How it works

Three steps, nothing permanent until you say so.

01 — Scan

Pick a folder, a drive, or your whole PC

Duplicate Finder hashes every file to find exact matches — not just similar names or sizes.

02 — Compare

See both copies side by side

File size, modified date, and a live preview for images, PDFs, Word docs, and Excel sheets — before you decide anything.

03 — Reclaim

Keep one, trash the rest

Duplicates go to the Recycle Bin, never a permanent delete. Change your mind anytime.

What it does

Built for actually finding duplicates, not guessing.

Byte-for-byte matching

Every file is hashed, so renamed or relocated copies still get caught — not just files with matching filenames.

Live previews

Images, PDFs, Word documents, Excel sheets, and code files render right in the comparison view.

Recycle Bin safe

Every delete goes through Windows' own Recycle Bin. Nothing is ever permanently removed by the app itself.

Scan a folder or a whole drive

From one Downloads folder to your entire C:\ drive, at whatever scope you choose.

FAQ

Before you download

Will it delete files I actually need?

Only files you explicitly mark, and only after you've compared them side by side. Matches are found by hashing file contents, so only true byte-for-byte duplicates ever show up — and every delete goes to the Recycle Bin, not a permanent removal.

Does it work on Mac or Linux?

Not yet — Duplicate Finder is Windows-only for now.

What happens after the 14-day trial?

The app locks scanning until you enter a license key. Your trial data and settings aren't affected — activating a key just unlocks it again.

Why does Windows show a warning when I install it?

Because the app isn't yet signed with a paid code-signing certificate — something most solo developers skip before their first sales. Windows flags any unrecognized publisher this way, whether the software is safe or not; it's not a judgment on this specific app. Click "More info" then "Run anyway" to continue. The source code is public on GitHub if you'd like to check what it does before installing.
